title: Lucena: building the bridge, which positions win?
outcomes: Recognises in unlabeled rook endings whether a pawn on the seventh with the king in front wins
Separates winning positions from rook-pawn positions that the tablebase gives as draws
Checks the cut-off and the file of the pawn before choosing a plan

steps.text: In **Lucena: building the bridge** you learned the bridge. Now the positions come without a label, and you decide before you move whether the bridge works. Check three things: is the enemy king **cut off** from the pawn, is the pawn on the **a- or h-file**, and who is to move?

**Conditions.** The pawn stands on the seventh, your king is in front of it and the enemy king is cut off. **When it fails:** on the a- or h-file, the same material can be a draw, as the next pair shows. Rule of thumb: with a rook pawn, do not assume the bridge works; with another pawn, still check the cut-off.

steps.title: Same idea, different file
steps.prompt: Predict each result for White to move, then check.

steps.title: King beside the pawn: not cut off
steps.prompt: Here the enemy king is not cut off; it stands next to the pawn. Only the side to move differs. Predict each result, then check.
Which of the three questions did you ask first: the cut-off, the file of the pawn, or whose move? Which one would have saved you in the position you got wrong?
